raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Settle in.","source_id":"GLUE_PACING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"You're starting in the Île de la Cité, right at Pont Neuf — take a moment to take it in.","source_id":"SYNTHESIZED_OPENER","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look to the middle of the bridge, at Henri IV on his horse — that bronze has been hiding things since 1818.","source_id":"GLUE_STAGING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The first statue here was torn down in 1792 and melted down in the Revolution.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["b0fed33f-085e-44a7-876f-e27a789cc69f"]},{"text":"When the Bourbon kings returned, Parisians paid to rebuild it in 1818, by public subscription.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The bronze came from melting down a statue of Desaix, and the new figure was cast from a surviving mould of the old one.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Before they sealed it, the sculptor François-Frédéric Lemot slipped four boxes inside.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"One held a life of Henri IV, one a 17th-century parchment certifying the original, one an account of how the new statue was commissioned, and one the names of everyone who had chipped in.","source_id":"c4cd77d6-2377-4371-b394-fb724d0d47ac","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"But those weren't the only secrets in there.","source_id":"b0fed33f-085e-44a7-876f-e27a789cc69f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"The anti-Royalist who cast the replacement smuggled a little statuette of Napoleon into the horse's belly — found only recently, during restoration.","source_id":"b0fed33f-085e-44a7-876f-e27a789cc69f","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Now the bridge itself.","source_id":"00ff73fc-18f6-4723-9cd4-97e002a55ed0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Pont Neuf means New Bridge, yet it's the oldest bridge still standing in Paris.","source_id":"00ff73fc-18f6-4723-9cd4-97e002a55ed0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["57eb7b3c-761a-424e-9618-07b61ff3dfae"]},{"text":"Henri IV built it — twelve graceful arches — and for its day the whole thing was radical.","source_id":"00ff73fc-18f6-4723-9cd4-97e002a55ed0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Every other bridge was packed with houses; this one was open stone, the first in Paris built that way.","source_id":"57eb7b3c-761a-424e-9618-07b61ff3dfae","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0,"also_cites":["00ff73fc-18f6-4723-9cd4-97e002a55ed0"]},{"text":"He was one of the city's first great town-planners, and he'd come to inspect the work, once leaping clean over an unfinished arch to the workmen's delight.","source_id":"00ff73fc-18f6-4723-9cd4-97e002a55ed0","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Look along the sides for the semicircular bays — those were market stalls once, worked by teeth-pullers, quack doctors and other hawkers.","source_id":"57eb7b3c-761a-424e-9618-07b61ff3dfae","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Just off the bridge lies the Place Dauphine, and once a year it became an open-air art show.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"On the Petite Fête-Dieu — the Small Corpus Christi, eight days after the main feast — young painters hung their canvases there from six in the morning until noon.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"It was an unofficial salon, a rare chance for unknowns to get noticed, a forerunner of the Salon des Refusés that later sparked the Impressionists.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"In 1720 a twenty-two-year-old, the son of the man who kept the king's billiards, showed an antique bas-relief here.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"J.-B. Vanloo stopped, studied it a long while, saw real quality, bought it, and took the young man under his wing.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Eight years on, that painter was Vanloo's colleague at the Academy of Painting — Jean-Baptiste-Siméon Chardin.","source_id":"70582f12-4829-4b52-8dfd-9f3672362754","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"Steps beside the statue drop down to the square du Vert Galant.","source_id":"1311c7fd-d25d-492b-b51c-acf1d91cabf7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That's where Jacques de Molay, Grand Master of the Templars, was burnt at the stake, cursing the kings as the flames took him.","source_id":"1311c7fd-d25d-492b-b51c-acf1d91cabf7","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":0},{"text":"That's Pont Neuf — the New Bridge that turned out to be the oldest, still keeping its secrets.","source_id":"GLUE_CLOSING","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":0}]}
